announcements.text: Raytheon Co., Marlborough, Massachusetts, has been awarded an $8,000,000,000 maximum ceiling, cost-plus-fixed-fee, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for the procurement of terminal developmental modernization, production restart services, and technical studies associated with Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center’s Strategic Communications Terminals. Work will be performed at Marlborough, Massachusetts; and Largo, Florida, and is expected to be completed by Oct. 12, 2036. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $800,000 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center, Hanscom Air Force Base, Massachusetts, is the contracting activity (FA2293-27-D-B001).

announcements.text: L3Harris Technologies Inc., Colorado Springs, Colorado, has been awarded a $33,141,075 modification (P00380) to previously awarded contract FA8823-20-C-0004 for the Unified Messaging System effort. announcements.text: Leidos Inc., Reston, Virginia, was awarded a $317,986,855 firm-fixed-price contract (HT003826DE014) to provide essential system reintegration, software licensing, and hosting services for the electronic health record system known as MHS GENESIS. MHS GENESIS is a critical defense business system. This contract was awarded as a sole-source bridge. This sole-source bridge contract will reduce in scope during the 12-month period and will facilitate transition to other service contractors while also establishing direct government relationships to solution providers. This award will be funded by fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds. The place of performance is Reston, Virginia. The period of performance is July 29, 2026, to Jan. 28, 2028. The Defense Health Agency, Defense Healthcare Management Systems Contracting Division, Arlington, Virginia, is the contracting activity. (Awarded Sept. 28, 2026).

announcements.text: Huntington Ingalls Inc.-Newport News Shipbuilding, Newport News, Virginia, is awarded a $56,178,573 cost-plus-fixed-fee contract to support engineering, technical, design agent, and design transfer activities for nuclear submarine capabilities and their sustainment, in support of Foreign Military Sales (FMS) requirements. This contract includes an option which, if exercised, would bring the cumulative value of this contract to $91,142,608. Work will be performed in Newport News, Virginia (88%); and various foreign locations (12%). Work is expected to be completed by September 2027. If the option is exercised, work will continue through September 2028. No U.S. funding is included in this contract. Foreign Partner funds in the amount of $19,115,000 were obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was not competitively procured in accordance with 10 U.S. Code 3204(a)(1) (only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements). Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N00024-27-C-2133).

announcements.text: Raytheon Co., Marlborough, Massachusetts, is awarded $15,078,910 for firm-fixed-price delivery order 00383-27-F-NE00 under previously awarded basic ordering agreement N00383-25-D-NE01 in support of fulfilling 419 requirements (46 National Item Identification Numbers used on the MK-99 fire control system, AN/SPY-1 (AN – Army Navy Joint Electronics Type Designation Systems; S – Water/Surface Ship; P – Radar; Y – Surveillance and Control) Transmitter Group and AN/SPY-3 Multifunction Radar systems. The 419 requirements are a result of the Commander, Naval Surface Force Surface Warfare Officer (SWO) Surface Force North Star goal of 75 mission capable ships. These initiatives include fleet stocking increases from allowancing remodeling efforts for operational availability and endurance supply, allowance change requests, maintenance activities, and forward deployed site stock level increases. The delivery order does not include an option provision. Work will be performed in Andover, Massachusetts (95%); and Chesapeake, Virgina (5%). Work is expected to be completed by December 2034. Fiscal 2026 working capital funds (Navy) in the amount of $15,078,910 will be obligated at the time of award and funds will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. One source was solicited for this sole-source requirement pursuant to the authority set forth in 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1) and one offer was received. Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon Systems Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity (00383-27-F-NE00).

announcements.text: BAE Systems Maritime Solutions Jacksonville LLC, Jacksonville, Florida, was awarded a $796,146 firm-fixed-price contract action for maintenance, modernization and repair of USS Thomas Hudner (DDG 116) Fiscal 2027 Docking Restricted Availability. The scope of this acquisition includes all labor, supervision, equipment, production, testing, facilities, and quality assurance necessary to prepare for and accomplish the Chief of Naval Operations Availability for critical modernization, maintenance, and repair programs. This contract includes options which, if exercised, would bring the cumulative value of this contract to $106,826,091. Work will be performed in Mayport, Florida, and is expected to be completed by January 2028. Fiscal 2025 other procurement, (Navy) funds in the amount of $796,146, are obligated, of which no funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively solicited, with one proposal received in response. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N0002427C4438). (Awarded Oct. 9, 2026).
